paper_metadata.title: Influence of magnetic arc oscillation and current pulsing on microstructure and high temperature tensile strength of alloy 718 TIG weldments

evidence.quote: Alloy 718 is a nickel based precipitation-hardenable superalloy
The chemical composition (wt.%) of the material alloy 718 used in the present study was Ni 53, Cr 18.2, Nb 5.08, Mo 3.13, Ti 0.97, Al 0.51, Si 0.12, C 0.02, B 0.003, S 0.002, P 0.005, Fe balance.

Among direct aged welds, continuous current weld exhibited lumpy Laves particles compared with welds prepared using magnetic arc oscillation and pulsed current techniques.
Among the direct aged weld fusion zones, magnetic arc oscillated welds exhibited refined and less interconnected Laves phase.
Laves phase was discrete and lower in amount in pulsed current welds in relation with continuous current welds.
The major difference between direct aged and solution treated and aged welds was the presence of additional phase δ in the form of needles in the solution treated and aged welds.
Magnetic arc oscillated welds had finer δ needles and lower amount of Laves phase compared with the other two welds.
The major difference between direct aged and solution treated and aged welds was the presence of additional phase δ in the form of needles in the solution treated and aged welds.
The weld fusion zone had a dendritic structure with the interdendritic regions etching dark.
The weld fusion zone had a dendritic structure with the interdendritic regions etching dark.
The solution treated and aged welds exhibited similar dendritic structures.

mechanisms.name: dendrite fragmentation and increased cooling rate by magnetic arc oscillation

evidence.quote: The magnetic arc oscillation breaks the dendrite branches that are formed during cooling of the molten weld pool. These broken dendrites act as favorable nucleating sites resulting in increased cooling rates of the weld pool.

mechanisms.name: reduced cooling rate due to higher heat input suppressing current pulsing benefit

evidence.quote: On one hand, the current pulsing increased cooling rate and on the other hand, the higher heat input used in the process lowered the cooling rate. So the full benefit of current pulsing in breaking the dendrite could not be realized.

mechanisms.name: Laves phase depletion of strengthening elements and brittle cracking

evidence.quote: The Laves is not only brittle but also weakens the dendrite core by depleting useful strengthening alloying elements.

mechanisms.name: dislocation pileup and back stress by discrete dispersed hard phase

evidence.quote: Discrete and dispersed hard phase can resist the dislocation motion by dislocation pileup and increases the back stress, which restricts the yielding of the material. It can also delay the void coalescence during tensile plastic deformation, resulting in higher tensile strength.
The probable mechanism may be decohesion of δ–matrix interface as δ is over aged incoherent phase of Ni3Nb (γ'').

mechanisms.name: delta phase precipitation by dissolution of Laves phase during slow solutionizing

evidence.quote: During solutionizing treatment the low heating rates result in precipitation of δ phase by dissolving the Laves phase.

The magnetic arc oscillation breaks the dendrite branches that are formed during cooling of the molten weld pool. These broken dendrites act as favorable nucleating sites resulting in increased cooling rates of the weld pool.

On one hand, the current pulsing increased cooling rate and on the other hand, the higher heat input used in the process lowered the cooling rate. So the full benefit of current pulsing in breaking the dendrite could not be realized.
The magnetic arc oscillation technique resulted in refined Laves phase with lesser interconnectivity.
The presence of Laves phase in all the weld fusion zones was responsible for the lower strength values of the welds compared with that of base metal at all test temperatures.

Among all direct aged weldments, magnetic arc oscillated weldments exhibited higher strength compared with the other two weldments due to discrete Laves phase in the microstructure of magnetic arc oscillated weld fusion zones.
The probable mechanism may be decohesion of δ–matrix interface as δ is over aged incoherent phase of Ni3Nb (γ'').
During solutionizing treatment the low heating rates result in precipitation of δ phase by dissolving the Laves phase.
